_why: Books whose stored description was still FLAN-T5 output, because neither the corpus nor the publisher passed the automatic gate. The model is gone from the product; its writing should go with it. So the sentences below were chosen by hand FROM THE BOOK'S OWN SOURCE SUMMARY -- by index, never retyped, so the text cannot drift from what the corpus actually says. Choosing which sentences to show is editorial work; writing new ones would be inventing provenance.
_format: catalogue id -> the sentence indices of verified_summary, in order, as split by whatitsabout_heuristic.split_sentences

_notes.119: Life of Pi -- the source opens on the book's three-part structure and the narrator's name. The premise everyone actually knows arrives at sentence 7, where the ship sinks, and sentence 8 puts Pi in the lifeboat with the tiger.
_notes.19: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix -- the source's first sentence runs two together with a lowercase 'when', and the ones after it open on 'After he' and 'A few days afterwards'. Sentences 11 and 12 begin on a proper noun and carry the book's actual conflict: Umbridge.
